sections.h2: Where is Huntsville, Alabama, and how big is it?
sections.html:
Huntsville is the largest city in Alabama and the county seat of Madison County, in the Appalachian part of north Alabama just south of the Tennessee line. The city has grown by annexation until it reaches into Limestone, Morgan and Marshall Counties as well, making it the only Alabama city located in four counties.

The area is 225.2 square miles, and its farthest east to west points are about 32 miles apart. The Census Bureau puts the 2025 population at 233,627, up from 215,006 in 2020, an increase of 8.7 percent.

  • Madison County holds most of the city
  • Parts lie in Limestone, Morgan and Marshall Counties
  • Elevation is about 577 feet
  • Monte Sano Mountain rises east of the city

Because of that spread, a seller should check the county on the deed. Madison County handles most Huntsville parcels, but a house in the western or southern annexed areas can belong to a different county for tax and recording purposes.

sections.h2: What is the history behind Huntsville?
sections.html:
Huntsville was settled around the Big Spring in 1805 and was named for pioneer John Hunt. It was incorporated as a town in 1811 and served for one year as Alabama's first capital after statehood in 1819.

Textile mills arrived in the late nineteenth century. The larger change followed World War II, when the Army set up Redstone Arsenal nearby and later research there turned toward rockets and space. Population jumped from 16,437 in 1950 to 72,365 in 1960, and passed 200,000 by 2020.

The city has historic districts that include Twickenham, Old Town and the Lowe Mill area. Homes in those districts date from the early 1800s to the early 1900s, and owners often have older plumbing, wiring and rooflines to deal with when they sell.

Aerospace and military technology drive the Huntsville economy, centered on Redstone Arsenal, Cummings Research Park, NASA's Marshall Space Flight Center and the Jetplex industrial park. Cummings Research Park is the second largest research park in the United States.

sections.h2: What does Huntsville weather mean for a house?
sections.html:
Huntsville has a humid subtropical climate, with more than 54 inches of rain a year and thunderstorms that can bring large hail, damaging straight line winds and tornadoes. Roofs and siding take the brunt of this.

The city lies in a region sometimes called Dixie Alley, which is more prone to violent, long track tornadoes than most of the country. On April 27, 2011, an EF5 tornado near Browns Ferry caused a multi day power outage across north Alabama and nine people were killed in Madison County. A tornado in November 1989 killed 21 people.

The land is also karst, with limestone bedrock and caves under the surface, and the city was founded around a karst spring. A buyer's inspection may look at drainage and the foundation for that reason.

Huntsville City Schools serves most of the city, with 23,939 students in the 2022 to 2023 year and six high schools. The part of Huntsville in Morgan County falls in the Morgan County School District, and a few parcels belong to the Madison County and Limestone County districts.

Higher education includes the University of Alabama in Huntsville, Alabama A&M University, which dates to 1875, Oakwood University, and J.F. Drake State Community and Technical College.

sections.h2: Which cities and towns border Huntsville?
sections.html:
Huntsville has borders surrounding both the cities of Madison and Triana, and it also borders Decatur, Athens, Owens Cross Roads and the town of Mooresville. Redstone Arsenal, Moores Mill, Meridianville and Lacey's Spring are census designated places on its edges.

Land around the city rises into hills and plateaus, including Monte Sano Mountain to the east, Wade Mountain to the north and Rainbow Mountain to the west. Hillside lots near those mountains drain differently from flat lots in the valley, and buyers may ask about that.

The city annexed about 21.5 square miles west into Limestone County in the early 2000s, added 1.03 square miles in Morgan County in 2018 and took in more than 1,000 acres in Marshall County in 2025. A house in one of those pockets uses the tax collector and probate office of its own county.

sections.h2: How wet is Huntsville, and what does that do to roofs and yards?
sections.html:
Huntsville receives its heaviest rain from November to May, when most months bring nearly or over 5 inches, and December is on average the wettest month. August to October runs slightly drier at under 3.6 inches a month.

The Wikipedia profile also records an EF2 tornado on January 21, 2010 and a 1995 tornado in the Anderson Hills subdivision that killed one person. Owners who have lived through storms often sell with roof patches or older shingles still on the house.

sections.h2: How are Huntsville property taxes billed and paid?
sections.html:
Madison County's tax collector bills Huntsville property tax. Taxes are due October 1 and delinquent after December 31, and Alabama law does not require a bill be mailed before they are delinquent, although the office sends a courtesy notice by October 1.

The county FAQ gives a rate of $5.80 per $100 of assessed value for property inside Huntsville city limits in its county table, with the regular homestead deduction applied after that. A $5 late fee applies after December 31, plus interest of 1 percent per month. The county holds an online tax lien sale and auction each May.

  • Office: Madison County Service Center, 1918 Memorial Parkway NW
  • Satellite: 100 Plaza Blvd, Madison
  • Hours: weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • Card payments carry a 2.75 percent fee plus $0.30
  • Personal checks are not accepted in April or May

The bill goes to the owner of record on October 1 of the prior year, so a seller can still receive a bill after closing. Ask the closing office to prorate it.

sections.h2: How is a Huntsville deed recorded?
sections.html:
The deed is recorded at the Madison County probate office, located at the Madison County Service Center, 1918 Memorial Parkway NW. New owners are told to confirm the deed is recorded and then assess the property with the tax assessor and claim exemptions.

Alabama also charges a recording tax of 50 cents per $500 of value, with proof of the actual purchase price attached, under Alabama Code 40-22-1. The tax is paid before the deed is accepted for record.

sections.h2: What do cash buyers mean for Huntsville sellers?
sections.html:
A cash buyer can close without a mortgage lender, so the sale does not depend on a loan appraisal. In a fast growing city like Huntsville, this suits owners who want certainty on timing.

  • Inherited homes with unpaid taxes
  • Rental properties with tenants in place
  • Houses with storm damage or old roofs
  • Owners moving for a job at Redstone or a plant

None of this replaces a title search or the payment of taxes owed at closing. Those steps happen in every sale.

faqs.q: What is the population of Huntsville, AL?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 233,627 residents as of July 1, 2025, up from 215,006 in the 2020 census.
Madison, Limestone, Morgan and Marshall Counties. Madison County holds most of the city and is the county seat.

faqs.q: When are Madison County property taxes due?
faqs.a: October 1, with delinquency after December 31. A $5 late fee and 1 percent monthly interest apply after that.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Huntsville?
faqs.a: At the Madison County probate office in the Madison County Service Center at 1918 Memorial Parkway NW, for parcels in Madison County.
Yes. The city is in a region known as Dixie Alley, and the 2011 Super Outbreak caused deaths in Madison County. Roof and storm damage are common reasons for repairs.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Huntsville house with tenants in it?
faqs.a: Yes. A buyer can purchase a rented house subject to the lease. Check the lease terms and give any required notices.
